title: Ordinary cartesian open-square direct-image mate is invertible
statement: Let $s:Y\to S$, $r:T\to S$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and $B\subseteq Y$ open. Put $P=Y\times_S T$, $P_B=B\times_S T$, $\pi:P\to Y$, $\pi_B:P_B\to B$ and $b:P_B\to P$ the pullback map. The square with $b,\pi_B,B\hookrightarrow Y,\pi$ is cartesian and $b$ is an open immersion. Let $\theta:b_*\pi_*\cong\pi_{B,*}B_*$ be the ordinary sectionwise direct-image composition comparison (functors composed in diagrammatic order). Transpose $\theta$ under restriction along $b$ and restriction to $B$, with their fixed ordinary module adjunctions [def-pc-kinjective-mayer-vietoris-data]. The resulting map $\pi_*|_B\to b^*\pi_{B,*}$ of ordinary module functors is a natural isomorphism. It is the identity on sections after the cartesian equality of opens.

proof.text: Cancel the bottom projection pullback square from the outer pullback square using IsPullback.of_bot. Base change of the open inclusion implies b is an open immersion. Construct theta with pushforwardComp and pushforwardCongr.

At an open W of B, expand the inverse mate into the restriction unit, theta, and restriction counit. The underlying abelian-group map is restriction along b image pi_B inverse W = pi inverse (B image W), by image_preimage_eq_preimage_image_of_isPullback. Compose the three restrictions using functoriality; the arrows are equal because opens form a thin category. Restriction along an equality is invertible. Both forgetful functors reflect isomorphisms, so each module component, and then the natural transformation, is invertible.
